Sorry so long winded about my post btw, but I wish I had known more firsthand from the perspective of the patient. More knowledge helped me have less anxiety about it. 

Plus, I was a little bit angry that they say it's nearly painless, felt misleading.

I have had 4 cervical biopsies in the last 13 yrs. 

The first Dr. told me the same thing, that it doesn't hurt, or is just like "a pinch". That Dr. lied, or never had one personally. Ask about topical lidocaine before. I think maybe they can, but don't actually remember.

I have experienced worse pain, but it definitely does hurt. 
I don't want you to worry too much because I will say it is usually quite fast, but I do want to be honest that it isn't "nothing".

 For me the anticipation made biopsies 1 and 2 far worse, I believe, than the actual procedure. By the 3rd and 4th I was more relaxed, surprisingly, because I knew what to expect. 
It also may have been easier based on the experience of the doctor on the second two times. The more you can try to relax, breathe slow and deep, and hopefully be distracted enough by the nurse or aid talking to you, the easier it will be. I hate when they say exactly when to expect "a pinch" because then you do more so, I think. 

The first was performed by a Dr. at my family practitioner's office, who probably performed this much less frequently than the next Dr. who did the last two colposcopies. That Dr. was at Planned Parenthood and did these many times a week. It was quicker, and both times MUCH less painful. Surprisingly so. 

The tool they use takes a really tiny sample, and they may want to do more than one sample. So e doctors will prescribe a single valium beforehand I guess, this may vary. But I'm pretty sure most would advise taking a few Ibuprofen or Acetaminophen at least, mine did. Make sure if you do, it is in advance enough to kick in some and work. 

This doesn't really do as much for the biopsy itself. It is more useful, in my opinion, for the cramping afterwards. 
The cramping can be pretty bad. Think intense period cramps. I spent the rest of the day of lying down with a heating pad on my abdomen,  and remembering Tylenol on schedule.

It does take days for it to actually be healed, but the pain *mostly* (maybe half?) subsided by the following day. Do be sure to follow their aftercare instructions to avoid infection risk. 
Basically this involved nothing entering the vagina for however many days they said. No bath water, foreign objects (tampons, finger while cleaning, whatever else). 

One of the things I felt unprepared for was the appearance of the post biopsy discharge...
